chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from 'Isam ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Aisha said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'The people of Barirah stipulated their manumission (wala') [for themselves].' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wala' (right of manumission) belongs to the one who manumits.'

key_terms.اشْتَرَوْا: They purchased/stipulated (in the context of buying the right).
key_terms.الْوَلَاءُ: The right of manumission or patronage, referring to the legal bond between a freed slave and their master.
key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a specific female slave mentioned in the context of this ruling.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling regarding the right of manumission (wala') for a freed slave?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the foundational legal principle of *al-wala' li-man a'taq* (the right of manumission belongs to the manumitter), clarifying that this right is inherent to the act of freeing rather than a negotiable commodity. The Prophet’s response to Aisha’s report regarding Barirah’s stipulation underscores that while parties may agree on other terms, the *wala'* relationship remains exclusively tied to the one who grants freedom, a ruling widely accepted across Shia and Sunni jurisprudence. This incident highlights the Prophet’s authority to override customary stipulations when they conflict with divine legal principles regarding social and economic ties post-emancipation.
